description: Ranking v1 for the site universe. Data only: the owner tunes weights, curves and exclusion rules here, with no code change. A score adds weighted fit evidence; it never measures buying interest. Each component value is in [-1, 1] and the weights are points that sum to 100.
score_meaning: Points of fit evidence for an Arm Decision Proof design partner (a site with a rigid-object task for a fixed arm first). A score is not a measure of buying interest.

fixed_arm_machine_tending.note: First target of the Arm Decision Proof: one fixed arm and a rigid part at a machine.

kitting_assembly.note: Rigid parts into kits or fixtures; a fixed arm can do it.

palletizing_depalletizing.note: Rigid cases at the end of a line; a fixed arm can do it.

sorting_pick_and_place.note: A fixed arm at induction or a sorter; polybags are deformable.

mobile_manipulator_case_picking.note: Mobile manipulation is in scope; totes and cases are rigid.

truck_trailer_unloading.note: Rigid boxes, but a mobile base and high mix.

food_prep_manipulation.note: A fixed arm over a line, but most food items are deformable and hygiene rules apply.

recycling_sorting.note: A fixed arm over a conveyor; the objects are crushed and mixed.

lab_sample_handling.note: Candidate row (no sites until activated): rigid labware with a fixed arm.

shelf_restocking.note: Mobile manipulation in stores; taxonomy notes no verified US restocking deployment.

hospital_logistics.note: Mostly navigation and delivery, with little manipulation.

harvesting_greenhouse.note: Candidate row (no sites until activated): deformable produce.

bimanual_folding.note: Deformable textiles. Deformable work is frozen under the Arm Decision Proof (AGENTS.md).

hotel_delivery.note: Candidate row (no sites until activated): navigation only.

autonomous_cleaning.note: Candidate row (no sites until activated): navigation only, not a manipulation target.

site_type_weight_notes.plant_chemical_pharma: Process plants handle bulk material; robot tasks are mostly packaging at the end of the line.
site_type_weight_notes.plant_primary_metal: Mills and foundries are hot and heavy; casting finishing is the robot task.
site_type_weight_notes.drycleaning_laundry_service: NAICS 812320 is mostly small storefront dry cleaners.

capability_scope.note: A site's capabilities come from its site types. OpenStreetMap types of unknown use add capabilities only when the site has no specific site type. A capability that only a secondary site type supports (for example a warehouse code on a plant) is multiplied by the factor.

size.note: Peak at 100-1,000 annual average employees (OSHA ITA). Values below 50 and above 2,500 employees are penalties. Interpolation is linear in log10 of the x value and clamped at both ends.

task_evidence.note: NAICS codes that name the task of a capability. The longest matching prefix of the site's own NAICS codes wins; a capability without a match gets the default. Values below the default are evidence against the task.

fixed_arm_machine_tending.label: Turned products, screws, nuts and bolts
Plastic film, sheet and bags (continuous extrusion)
Plastic pipe and profile shapes (continuous extrusion)
Metalworking machinery: molds, dies, tools and machine tools
Engines, turbines and power transmission equipment
Semiconductors and electronic components (tools already automated)

operator_scale.note: Sites in the snapshot that share the operator's key (normalized operator or name tokens). One site suggests a local decision maker; a large chain decides centrally. Interpolation is linear in log10 of the site count.
operator_scale.numbered_unit_note: A name that carries a unit number (a leading 3-6 digit number that is not an address: no thoroughfare word follows it and it is not the site's own house number; a number sign with two or more digits; or 'Store' with a number) is a unit of a chain, so the site count is at least this number.

activity_evidence.note: The strongest available evidence that the site operates now.

ownership.note: Public-sector sites (federal, state, county and city) buy through procurement and decide slowly.

source_corroboration.note: Independent public sources that list the site.

exclusions.label: Operator with an in-house robotics program
exclusions.reason: The operator builds its own robots for these tasks, so it is unlikely to need an outside design partner.

evidence.note: Amazon Robotics (formerly Kiva Systems) builds Amazon's warehouse robots in house.

exclusions.label: Operator with a known fleet-scale robot deployment for these tasks
exclusions.reason: The operator already deploys robots for these tasks at scale with a named vendor, so a new design partnership is unlikely.

evidence.note: Taxonomy evidence: DHL signed for more than 1,000 more Boston Dynamics Stretch robots.

entries.label: FedEx (Berkshire Grey and Plus One robots)
Walmart (Symbotic palletizing systems in regional DCs)
Sam's Club (Walmart; BrainOS robots in every US club)
Mercado Libre (Agility Digit in San Antonio)

exclusions.label: Defense or ITAR-heavy prime or site
exclusions.reason: ITAR controls and site security restrict outside capture, data handling and robot evaluation, so the site cannot be a first design partner.

evidence.note: International Traffic in Arms Regulations (22 CFR 120-130).
Directorate of Defense Trade Controls, which administers ITAR registration.

naics.note: Aircraft (336411; this also covers civil aircraft makers), guided missiles and space vehicles (336414, 336415, 336419), military armored vehicles (336992) and ammunition and ordnance (332992-332994).

exclusions.label: Office or headquarters
exclusions.reason: An office or headquarters has no physical robot task on site; the operating sites are elsewhere.

evidence.note: NAICS 551114: corporate, subsidiary and regional managing offices.

naics.note: Primary codes only: a plant often lists 551114 as a secondary code for its on-site offices.

phrases.note: Only the primary site name. A name that also names a physical operation (an office and warehouse, a retail support center, which is a distribution center) is kept.

exclusions.label: Inactive in EPA FRS
exclusions.reason: Every EPA FRS program record for the site is closed, so the site may no longer operate. An OSHA ITA filing for 2024 or later, or a listing in the USDA FSIS inspection directory, overrides this: the establishment reported workers that year or is under inspection now.

evidence.note: The FRS environmental interest file gives each program record an ACTIVE_STATUS; the snapshot marks a site inactive when every status is terminated, expired, inactive or closed.

exclusions.label: No street address and no coordinates
exclusions.reason: A site without a street address or coordinates cannot be found for a capture visit.

evidence.note: Site universe design v1: each candidate must be a locatable physical site.
